newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Primagaz says good Q2 made up for slow Q1.
newsitem.headline: Primagaz says good Q2 made up for slow Q1.

text.p: The chief executive of Hungarian liquefied petroleum gas distributor Primagaz Rt, Zoltan Szemmelveisz, said on Wednesday that a better than expected second quarter made up for a slow first quarter of 1997.
"The second quarter of the year brought cold weather and lower international gas prices compared with a mild first quarter and more expensive gas," Szemmelveisz told a news conference.

Primagaz released its first-half unaudited IAS results on Wednesday reporting a net profit of 662 million forints ($3.4 million) on net sales of 9.62 billion forints compared with a net profit of 479 million forints on net sales of 7.88 billion forints in the same period of 1996.
Szemmelveisz said the company has probably maintained the 72 percent market share that it had at the end of 1996, the latest figure available.
He also said that Primagaz has a storage capacity of 12,000 cubic meters or 6,000 tonnes, that means a reserve of 10 days' supply during peak winter days and some 15 days during the summer.
He said Primagaz plans to increase its storage capacity in 1998 or 1999 but added that even at present, using alternative storage such as railway cars, it has reserves of 12,000 tonnes.
Szemmelveisz said that in accord with an agreement with the Consumer Protection Agency last December, Primagaz spent some 230 million forints on quantitative control of its gas cylinders.
"We supplied all 3,600 retail stations with scales and have also installed an electronic scale on one filling line and other two are being installed," Szemmelveisz said.
He added that by autumn all production lines will have shrink-wrapping equipment to ensure the cylinders are not tampered with.
Consistent with Primagaz's business policy of informing only shareholders about the company's full-year targets, Szemmelveisz did not give any profit forecast for 1997.

Primagaz is 64.7 percent owned by Netherland's Pam Gas BV, Oesterreichische Kontrollbank has a five percent stake, Creditanstalt Bankverein owns four percent and the rest is owned by small shareholders.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Primagaz shares closed at 10,900 forints, down 400.
-- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($ = 197.1 Hungarian Forints)
